-71.05500,42.35100.name: Circle Surrogacy
-71.05500,42.35100.state: Boston — with New York, San Francisco, Washington DC and London
-71.05500,42.35100.desc: Founded in 1995 by a lawyer who had children through surrogacy himself, and now one of the largest agencies in the United States: over 4,000 babies, more than 3,000 surrogates, partnerships with nearly 400 fertility clinics, and intended parents in 70 countries. It sells a fixed-price programme at around $189,500 and employs its own lawyers, social workers, insurance and financial staff rather than referring out. Its own state guidance is the useful document: in Massachusetts, where it is headquartered, it notes there are no laws regulating surrogacy and that professionals have established agreed procedures among themselves. An industry writing its own procedure where statute is silent is the condition this whole facet operates in, and here it is stated plainly by a participant.

111.75190,40.84140.name: Jinyu Bio-Technology
111.75190,40.84140.desc: One of the largest producers of animal vaccines in China and among the homegrown companies that dominate a market foreign firms have struggled to enter. The market's shape is set by policy rather than by demand: porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome and hog cholera were removed from compulsory vaccination in 2017, which moved them into the higher-margin market-priced category, and African swine fever then collapsed the pig herd and with it the hog vaccine share. A company in this position is exposed to two things at once — a ministry's list and an epidemic — and neither is a commercial decision.
